blurb:
Melt Yard is a solid pick for a casual lunch or a low-key dinner, especially if you've got a group with different appetites. The service gets consistently good marks, and it's the kind of place that works well for families. Not trying to be anything fancy, just doing its thing on Whitlock Ave.

Fair warning: a few people mention the food can run on the greasy side, which is worth knowing going in. That said, the same folks say they'd come back and try something different, so it's not a dealbreaker by any stretch.

Fridays and Saturdays they're open until 10pm if you're looking for a later dinner spot.

blurb:
This place has become a regular stop for me when I want a solid, no-fuss Middle Eastern meal without any fanfare. It's easygoing, welcoming, and the kind of spot that works whether you're grabbing a quick lunch solo or bringing the family for an easy weeknight dinner. Nothing pretentious about it, which is honestly part of the appeal.

The shawarma is what most people are coming in for, and it earns the reputation. The falafel is also worth ordering if you're leaning vegetarian. They've got dessert options too if you want to finish it off right.

They're open every day from 10am to 9pm, so there's really no excuse not to try it.

blurb:
Marietta Square Market is a food hall, which means it solves one of the most common family dinner problems: nobody can agree on what to eat. Twenty vendors under one roof, all doing different things. My wife and I have ended up here more than once just because it's easy and there's always something for everyone.

The setup makes it a great spot for a casual lunch, a weeknight dinner when nobody feels like cooking, or really any time you want options without having to commit to one restaurant. The variety is the whole point here, not any single dish.

Fridays and Saturdays they're open until 10pm, so it works for an evening out around the Square too.

blurb:
If you've never done an all-you-can-eat Brazilian barbecue spot, Rio is a great place to start. It's relaxed, not stuffy, and the kind of meal where you show up hungry and leave in a different condition entirely. Good for a Saturday lunch with the family or a dinner when you just want to eat well without overthinking a menu.

The barbecue is the main event, but the cheese bread has a serious following and for good reason. If you're in the mood for something heartier, the feijoada stew is worth trying. They also do breakfast, which is a little unexpected but apparently people love it.

Friday and Saturday they're open until 11pm, so it works for a later dinner too.

blurb:
Almost five stars on nearly 19,000 reviews. That's not an accident. Douceur De France is a French bakery that actually delivers, and my wife and I have made it a Saturday morning habit more times than I can count. The place is bright, the smell hits you before you're even through the door, and it never gets old.

The baguettes are the real deal. The quiches are worth knowing about if you're there for something more substantial. And the petits fours make a solid treat to grab on the way out. It's the kind of place where you go in for one thing and leave with four.

Sundays they close at 3:30pm, so don't sleep too late if that's your plan.
